note: Seats per ParlGov, which breaks the pre-election centre-right (Lega/Forza Italia/FdI/UC) and centre-left (PD/SVP/+Europa/IdV/CD/one-seat) coalitions down to individual constituent-party seat counts. Conte I government (confirmed via ParlGov cabinet-parties) = M5S + Lega only; Forza Italia and Fratelli d'Italia, despite contesting as part of the pre-election centre-right coalition, did NOT enter the Conte I cabinet. CORRECTION (2026-09-14): the prior version was missing a party and had one wikidata_id gap, both now fixed: (1) added 'Together' (Insieme/IEI - Italian Socialist Party + Federation of the Greens + Civic Area, 190,601 votes, 1 seat), which ParlGov lists under an unnamed generic 'one-seat' row (party id 2302, description 'parties that won one seat ... and less than one percent vote share') - identified via cross-referencing the vote count (190,601) against the English Wikipedia results table, confirmed wikidata_id Q46624077 (label 'Together', Italian electoral list, inception 14 Dec 2017, dissolved 2 Dec 2018) directly on wikidata.org; without it seats summed to 629 instead of 630. (2) 'Democratic Centre' (CD, 1 seat) resolved to wikidata_id Q1952211 ('Democratic Centre'/'Centro Democratico', political party in Italy, inception 28 Dec 2012 - matches Bruno Tabacci's party), confirmed directly on wikidata.org, disambiguated from Q25406692 (Ecuador), Q15909095/Q28483994/Q55471857 (Spain/Colombia variants), Q15456227 (a later 2019 parliamentary-group rebrand) and other same-named items. Also note: ParlGov's 'IdV' (Italy of Values) row (2 seats, 178,107 votes) actually represents the joint 'Popular Civic List' (AP+CpE+IdV+UpT+IP, led by Beatrice Lorenzin) per Wikipedia's results table - ParlGov's own choice of label, kept as-is per the 'follow ParlGov's granularity' convention used throughout this file, wikidata_id Q47768 is for IdV specifically not the joint list. Seats now sum to 630/630.
